title: Numbers: agreement, age, prices, time, dates

questions.prompt: У нас ___ дочь и два сына.
questions.hint: We have one daughter and two sons.
questions.explain: один agrees in gender: дочь is feminine → одна.
Compound numbers follow the last word: двадцать один → год, just as after один.
The last word is три → genitive singular: года.
11–14 always take the genitive plural (лет), even though they end in 1–4.
Numbers ending in 5–9 or 0 (пять, десять, сто, пятьсот…) take the genitive plural: рублей.

questions.hint: How many sisters do you have?
questions.explain: сколько + genitive plural for things you can count: сестра → сестёр.

questions.hint: There are two new phones on the table.
questions.explain: After 2–4, an adjective with a masculine or neuter noun goes into the genitive plural: два новых телефона.

questions.hint: I was born on the fifth of May.
questions.explain: On which date? → genitive of the ordinal, no preposition: пятого мая.

questions.hint: Let's meet at five past five.
questions.explain: Minutes past the hour count towards the next hour (ordinal in the genitive): 5:05 = пять минут шестого.
книга is feminine → две; два is for masculine and neuter nouns.
Age = dative + number + год / года / лет, with no verb: мне двадцать пять лет.

questions.hint: There were five people at the meeting.
questions.explain: After a number, 'people' is человек: пять человек (людей goes with много, мало).
евро never changes: один евро, три евро, сто евро.

questions.prompt: Today is the first of December.
questions.explain: Today's date: neuter ordinal (число is understood) + month in the genitive.

questions.prompt: We have two cats and five dogs.
answer: У нас две кошки и пять собак.
У нас два кота и пять собак.
У нас есть две кошки и пять собак.
У нас есть два кота и пять собак.
questions.explain: две + genitive singular (кошки), пять + genitive plural (собак).
